content.text: FOR DECADES, WOMEN ACROSS THE GLOBE HAVE BEEN FED A LIE.

content.html: The lie that the biblical woman is an oppressed woman.

This lie is as old as time; there is nothing new under the sun. The first feminists fought to be equal under the law, not to erase roles altogether. However, over the years, this has changed. The enemy has convinced young women that they must abandon their God-given calling within the home and flip their priorities backwards to appease the feminist hustler culture we see today.

Far too many Christian women today are eager to call themselves a feminist. The fear of the roles God has called women to is a direct act of unbelief and disobedience. We must not believe this fallen world’s definition of womanhood, and cling tightly to God’s truth.

content.quote: God created man and woman equal, but different. The Women of Virtue Movement is devoted to reassuring women around the globe that they do not need to suppress their feminine nature.

devotionals.title: Firm Foundations
devotionals.description: Weekly Devotionals for Women of Virtue

lessons.title: Defining Femininity
lessons.intro: Contrary to the blurred lines of the fallen world, the bible defines a woman quite clearly. Follow along to learn what God’s word has to say about the true woman.

sections.title: Creation and Identity
paragraphs: Genesis 1:27
— “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God he created him; Male and Female he created them.”
Both Women and Men share equal value in being created in God's image.
Genesis 2:22
— “And the rib that the Lord God had taken from the man he made into a Woman and brought her to the man.”
God intentionally formed womanhood.

sections.title: Character and Value
paragraphs: Proverbs 31:30
— “Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the lord is to be praised.”
True worth comes from honoring and fearing the Lord
Proverbs 14:1
— “Every wise woman buildeth her house; but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.”
A woman’s actions and attitude, both within the home and outside of it, have a profound impact.
Proverbs 31:25
— “Strength and honor are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.”
Character, virtue, and dignity define a powerful and capable woman.

sections.title: Roles and Distinction
paragraphs: Genesis 2:18
— “Then the lord God said, ‘It is not good for man to be alone, I shall make a helper fit for him.’”
The woman was designed as a partner and strong helper. {Ezer}
Ezer was often used to refer to God himself when he was called on for help and rescue.
Deuteronomy 22:5
— “A woman shall not wear a man’s garment, nor shall a man put on a woman’s cloak.”
Scripture continually affirms a clear distinction between male and female identities.

Amen 1928 Book of Common Prayer

lessons.title: Prayer Life and Church Community
lessons.introTitle: Women were never meant to face life alone.

sections.title: Prayer Life
paragraphs: 1 Thessalonians 5:16–18
“Rejoice always, pray continually, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.”
When you have a healthy prayer life, it is easier to feel more connected to Christ. Thus making it easier to trust that he is working in your favor.
Romans 12:12
“Rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, be constant in prayer.”
Scripture regularly reminds us to be — “constant in prayer.” We ought not to forsake building a personal relationship with the Lord through prayer.

sections.title: Church Community
paragraphs: Romans 12:4–5:
“For as in one body we have many members, and the members do not all have the same function, so we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another.”
Every woman brings her own unique set of gifts into the body of Christ.
Galatians 6:2:
“Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.”
When we are able to rely on each other’s shoulders, we lighten the load of each individual.
Hebrews 10:24–25:
“And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another.”
It is important for sisters in Christ to keep each other not only company, but accountable.

devotionals.title: The Virtous Heart
devotionals.description: Aligning our hearts with God's word.

lessons.title: Harden Not
lessons.intro: When we look around today, it seems that the entire world has gone dark. With increasing prevalence  of heinous crimes,vulgarity, and mental health disorders amongst younger generations, it's easy to feel like we are too far gone. But we must not lose the tenderness that the Lord has gifted us.

sections.title: Guard Your Heart
paragraphs:
Wise and Innocent 
Matthew 10:16 “Behold I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves, so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.”

A virtuous heart can be surrounded by the evils of this world, and fear not, because we know who is sending us. We are all called to be the light in the darkness. We should all be as eager as Isaiah to be sent out by the Lord.

Wellspring 
Proverbs 4:23 “Above all else guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.”

It's easy for this world to begin to infect our heart, but we must guard entry to preserve the tender nature God has blessed us with; to love God and to love our neighbor, even when we are amidst the darkness.

sections.title: Intentional Tenderness
paragraphs:
Poor and Needy
 Proverbs 31:20 “She opens her arms to the poor and extends her hands to the needy.”

This verse might make you think of volunteering at a homeless shelter or serving in a soup kitchen. These are beautiful acts of service to the kingdom, but this proverb runs much deeper than that. Sometimes it looks like being the first to volunteer to give someone a ride, or cooking a meal for someone going through a hard time. When we intentionally show up for others, regularly, it shapes our heart to look more like Christ’s. Lets be sure to be EAGER givers, in all aspects of life.

sections.title: Forgivness
paragraphs:
Avoiding revenge
 Leviticus 19:18 “Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against anyone among your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the Lord.”

When we begin to open our hearts and recognize that we are all children of the Lord, it becomes easier to forgive. “Love your neighbor as yourself” is God's second greatest commandment, and it comes without conditions. Regardless of whatever sins they have committed against you, the Lord commands us to forgive, that we may be forgiven.

Peace 
 Romans 12:18 “If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.”

“LIVE at peace.” This isn't just tolerating everyone, peace is within yourself, provided by the Lord. A virtuous heart has a peace that cannot be moved. When we lean on the Lord and not our own understanding, he is able to provide the kind of peace in your heart that leaves no room for grudges.

sections.title: REFLECTION QUESTIONS
paragraphs:
Search your heart:
 Are there any hard spots that you need to surrender to the Lord?
What are some ways you can serve gladly this week?
What does forgiveness entail? Think of someone who's deeply hurt you, have you genuinely forgiven them?

resource: Prayer: The Collect for Quinquagesima 1928 BCP

“O LORD, who has taught us that all our doings without charity are worth nothing; Send thy Holy Ghost, and pour into our hearts that most excellent gift of charity, the very bond of peace and all virtues, without which whosoever liveth is counted dead before tee. Grant this for thine only son Jesus Christ's sake. Amen.”

lessons.title: Denying Flesh
lessons.intro: It is easy to get consumed by self-interest and personal desires as a woman. We are given a passionate heart by design, to nurture and care for those around us. However, we often get caught up in emotional webs of our own weaving. When we are not grounded in the Lord, it's easy for those webs to ensnare rather than support us.

sections.title: Protection Not Punishment
paragraphs:
Fallen World 
Ephesians 6:12-13 "For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. Therefore put on the full armor of God..."

We cannot control the state of the fallen world, and the cycle of sin and death will continue until the Lord returns. However, he offers us protection and peace inside the storm. You WILL still be afflicted by the world, but our hope is not in this world, it is found only in Jesus Christ.

Lean not on your own understanding
 Proverbs 3:5-6 "Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways submit to him, and he will make your paths straight."

When we are leaning on our own understanding, it's easy for the outside world to cause us distress, both directly in your personal life and through what we see happening around the world. When we lean on the Lord, He will grant us a peace that no evil can disturb. The protection God offers is incomprehensible, he will guide our hearts and paths in the way of peace when we will put our trust in his plans.

sections.title: Disipline and Growth
paragraphs:
Creatures of habit 
1 Timothy 4:7-8 “Train yourself to be godly. For physical training is of some value, but godliness has value for all things”

We gain a virtuous heart through habit—it does not happen overnight. When we make it routine to spend time with the Lord, in prayer and through his word, we train our heart posture to lean on the Lord. Slowly these habits become a part of our character, molding our hearts and minds and allowing God to lead instead of our wayward flesh.

Feed your Spirit not your Flesh:
 Matthew 6:11 “Give us this day our daily bread”

What a profound grace, “daily bread.” God provides for today; physically, emotionally, financially, spiritually, every day. Take and eat God's word DAILY, sit with Him DAILY, surrender DAILY, and He will provide daily. We need not worry about the state of the world or our lives tomorrow, for today we are blessed.

sections.title: Iron Sharpens Iron
paragraphs:
Confession 
James 5:16 “Therfore confess your sins to eachother and pray for eachother so that you may be healed.”

We confess our sins to God for forgiveness, and we confess our sins to each other for healing. We ought not kick one another when we fall short, but we ought to hold each other accountable, that we may inherit the kingdom of God together. We love others as we love ourselves and we should work as one body to deny our flesh and keep our hearts focused on the Lord.

Bear one another's burdens 
 Galatians 6:2 “Carry one another's burdens, and in this you will fulfill the law of Christ.”

The word burden comes from the word “baros.” It means a heavy weight, something that's too heavy to carry alone. The world today can feel extremely heavy on the heart. When we bear it together, it can help us all get through today. Be eager to bear the burdens of your neighbor, and be eager to let those you trust bear yours.

sections.title: REFLECTION QUESTIONS
paragraphs: Is there anything your flesh is holding onto that the Lord has called you to let go of?
What practices can you add to your daily routine to train your heart for godliness?
Who can you go to when you've fallen short to sharpen you?

devotionals.title: Fruitful
devotionals.description: Fruitfulness is not about becoming a better Christian, it's about drawing so near to Christ that His character begins to show up in your actions and attitude. This week we are doing more than checking boxes, we are seeking God to cultivate the fruit of HIS Spirit in our everyday lives. When we abide in Him, we don't have to force the fruits, we bear them.

lessons.title: Fruit?
lessons.intro: It is called fruit—singular in the Greek: Karposs. It is one fruit, with nine characteristics, the characteristics of Christ. Being fruitful isn't a test, it's a transformation in us through the Holy Spirit. We can easily confuse our works with our fruit; works are actions, but the fruit is a state of being.

sections.title: THE 9 CHARACTERISTICS OF FRUIT
paragraphs:
LOVE (AGAPE)
Unconditional, selfless love.The kind that is sacrificial. The kind of love that a Father has for his Children. It is a choice, not a feeling.

JOY (CHARA)
A deep gladness because of who God is, not because of what's currently going on in our lives.

PEACE (EIRENE) 
Complete serenity because you have been joined to God.

Our peace does not come from worldly security, but rather from the security that God's promises to us are true and everlasting. Nothing that happens on this earth and in our daily lives can frustrate God’s plans for the end. God has already won, we are simply awaiting the feast.

FOREBEARANCE (MAKROTHUMIA)
The ability to be wronged without retaliation, to wait without growing bitter. Forbearance is a divine patience that comes only from the Lord.

When we are patient and forgiving towards others, we directly reflect the love of Christ. None of us DESERVE mercy, yet our Heavenly Father gives it every day. He never grows tired of forgiving us, we mustn't grow tired of forgiving each other.

KINDNESS (CHRESTOTES)
Often confused with niceness, true kindness actively seeks the best for others. Kindness is useful, benevolent, and willing to have a hard conversation if it helps someone heal or grow towards the Lord.

When we are kind to others, we show them the love of Christ. We must not lose true kindness in order to make others comfortable or happy. We must hold fast to God's truth and encourage each other daily to do the same.

GOODNESS (AGATHOSUNE) 
Moral integrity and courage rooted in the Lord.
As believers we are called to have a backbone, to do what IS right, not just what feels right. When Jesus flipped tables, he wasn't being nice, he was being GOOD.

FAITHFULNESS (PISTIS)
Loyalty and reliability, both towards the Lord and towards others.
When we have Faithfulness we can be trusted with the small and large things. Being faithful is a daily commitment between us and the Lord.

GENTLENESS (PRAUTES)
Gentleness is not weakness, it is strength used for good. Jesus could have called a legion of angels down to fight for Him, instead He touched lepers, washed feet, and ultimately let Himself be crucified on the cross, was He weak? Of course not.

We are called to be gentle. Gentle with others, gentle with ourselves. This isn't appeasement, nor is it being soft. It is the innate drive to have mercy with others, while still holding them fast to the truth, just as our Lord Jesus Christ has done towards us.

SELF-CONTROL (EGKRATEIA)
The ability to fight our flesh.
When we are close to the lord, and allow the spirit to guide us, we are able to control our fleshy desires and seek first the kingdom.

sections.title: REFLECTION QUESTIONS
paragraphs: What evidence of fruit do you see in those around you? In yourself?
How has the Lord shown fruit towards you recently?
How have you seen God’s fruit develop and ripen in you over the past few years?
Is there anything you don't quite understand about the fruit of the Spirit?

lessons.title: BEARING
lessons.introTitle: What does it mean to 'bear' Fruit?
lessons.intro: We've learned what the fruit is, but how does it actually look day to day in our lives? God does not say to “Act Fruitful” he calls us to BEAR it. When we are abiding in Christ; His word, His character, and HIS fruit begins to show up all around and within us.

sections.title: ABIDE
paragraphs: When we spend time with the Lord, through prayer and reading his word, he begins to mold us. Abiding isn't a checklist, its daily connection to our father. When you are connected to the vine, the fruit soon follows. We ought to cling tightly to the Lord, not as a demonstration for what we can do for Him, but rather what He can do in us.

Hosea 10:12
“Break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the Lord, that He may rain righteousness upon you”

sections.title: RECEIVE
paragraphs: Fruit is not something you work for, it is something you receive through the Lord. It is His fruit, not ours. We begin to receive fruit as the spirit transforms our hearts and minds. When we let God work in us, He begins to produce the fruit through us. An inner transformation occurs before the outward expression.

John 15:4-5
"Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit by itself, unless it abides in the vine, neither can you, unless you abide in me. I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing."

sections.title: PROVIDE
paragraphs: The fruit is not for the tree. The fruit the Lord produces in us  is not for ourselves, it is for the people passing by, and to spread seeds. We must use the fruit God has instilled in us through His holy vine in order to help, encourage, and grow those around us. By sharing our fruit with others, we are directly planting seeds and spreading the Gospel. Matthew states, “you shall know them by their fruit.” Our fruit should be evident to those around us, it's not a personal gift, but rather God using us as living instruments to love each other well.

1 Peter 4:10
"As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace:"

resource: The Collect For The Ninth Sunday After Trinity, American Book Of Common Prayer  (1928)

“Grant to us. Lord, we beseech thee, the Spirit to think and do always such things as are right; that we, who cannot do any thing that is good without thee, may by thee be enabled to live according to thy will; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen,”

lessons.title: ESSENTIAL
lessons.intro: It is essential that we develop a sisterhood with other faithful women of Christ. We were designed for it. We can see this innate communal structure modeled for us in the Trinity.  When we lack a meaningful relationship with our Sisters, it is easy for the enemy to isolate us and infiltrate our hearts and minds. We need our sisters to hold us fast to the Lord, and help us along the straight and narrow path

sections.title: DESIGN
paragraphs:
Genesis 1:26
“ And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”

When mankind was first created, we were modeled after God's own image. We were designed to have community with each other, just as the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit have community amongst themselves. We were never meant to do life alone.

sections.title: ISOLATION
paragraphs: When Eve was first tempted by the serpent, he isolated her. When we do not have the support of other strong-willed believers supporting us, it becomes easier for the enemy to isolate and deceive us

sections.title: ACCOUNTABILITY
paragraphs:
Proverbs 27:17
“As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.”

As believers, we need each other to hold us accountable. It is a great blessing to have a sister in Christ who is more concerned about your salvation and sanctification than your feelings and desires. We should surround ourselves with faithful and virtuous women who can help keep us on the right path.

sections.title: REFLECTION QUESTIONS
paragraphs: How have you been supported and uplifted by your sisters in Christ?
Do you ever feel isolated? If so, do you reach out to your sisters for encouragement?
How can you pursue meaningful relationships with women of the faith near you?

lessons.title: INTENTIONAL
lessons.intro: Not only do we need good sisters, but we need to BE good sisters. Everyone wants a village, but few want to be a villager. It doesn't come by accident, we build our sisterhood with intentionality. Being a good sister is a daily decision to love and support one another well.

sections.title: LOYALTY
paragraphs:
Proverbs 3:3
“Let love and faithfulness never leave you;  bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.”

Loyalty and faithfulness appear in the valley, not on the mountain top. We ought to cling to each other during the hard seasons, just as Naomi clung to Ruth when she was widowed and destitute. It's easy to be a good sister when everything is going according to our own plans, but we need to make the effort daily in the darkness to be a light to our sisters, during our troubles and theirs.

sections.title: HONOR AND TRUTH
paragraphs:
Ephesians 4:15-16
“ Instead, speaking the truth in love, we will grow to become in every respect the mature body of him who is the head, that is, Christ. 16 From him the whole body, joined and held together by every supporting ligament, grows and builds itself up in love, as each part does its work.”

To love our sisters well is to be honest with them. Speaking truth over your sister isnt shaming or belittling her, its holding her accountable and to a higher standard. Just as our Heavenly Father convicts and guides us, we must also lovingly correct each other, that we may fulfill the law of Christ, and inherit the kingdom together. Likewise, we ought to honor each other, never speaking ill or sharing behind each others backs. Ephesians 4:29 states, “ Do not let any unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building others up according to their needs, that it may benefit those who listen.” We are called to build each other up, not tear each other down with our words.

sections.title: COVER NOT COVET
paragraphs:
Luke 12:15
“And He said to them, "Take heed and beware of covetousness, for one's life does not consist in the abundance of the things he possesses."

James 2:14-16
 But if you harbor bitter envy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast about it or deny the truth.  Such “wisdom” does not come down from heaven but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic. For where you have envy and selfish ambition, there you find disorder and every evil practice. “

1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 
‘Rejoice always, pray continually, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.”

Coveting is not simply desiring the same things that someone else has, it stems from envy and pride. We need to be able to rejoice over our sister's rain during our drought. We should never be jealous or drawn to anger when the father is blessing someone else, instead we shall praise the Lord with them and cover them in prayer and gratitude.

sections.title: REFLECTION QUESTIONS
paragraphs: How can you support your sisters this week?
Search your heart, have you ever coveted your sister's blessings?
How can you show gratitude for the women God has placed in your life?

resource: The Collect for All Saints Day- American Book Of Common Prayer  (1928)

O ALMIGHTY God, who hast knit together thine elect in one communion and fellowship, in the mystical body of thy Son Christ our Lord; Grant us grace so to follow thy blessed Saints in all virtuous and godly living, that we may come to those unspeakable joys which thou hast prepared for those who unfeignedly love thee; through the same thy Son Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
